audits.title: Clinical Audit on Identification, Evaluation and Optimisation of Anti-Cholinergic Burden in Older Adults With Cognitive Impairment Referred to East Hub Older Adult Community Mental Health Team at BSMHFT
audits.standard: NICE guidelines on assessing and optimising anticholinergic burden
audits.setting: East Hub Older Adult Community Mental Health Team, BSMHFT

cycle1.result: 24% of patients with an ACB score greater than 3 had no documented assessment of anticholinergic burden or medication optimisation.

audits.other_findings: Findings disseminated Trust-wide and an ACB calculator (medichec.com) adopted before re-audit.
audits.citation: Bhattacharya S. Clinical Audit on Identification, Evaluation and Optimisation of Anti-Cholinergic Burden in Older Adults With Cognitive Impairment Referred to East Hub Older Adult Community Mental Health Team at BSMHFT. BJPsych Open. 2025;11(S1):S221-S221. doi:10.1192/bjo.2025.10558.

audits.title: A Prospective Audit Investigating How the Anticholinergic Effect of Medications on Cognition Is Assessed and Reduced in Patients Admitted to an Older Adult Ward in a Psychiatric Hospital
audits.standard: MediChec AEC score: individual AEC above 2 or total above 3 requires medication review; AEC recorded at admission, during admission and at discharge

cycle1.result: AEC documented for 22/24; 22.7% (n = 5) within 7 days of admission; no patient whose score indicated review had a documented medication review or follow-up AEC score.

audits.other_findings: AEC scores were recorded only by the lead pharmacist. Recommended a poster and adding AEC to the ward-round template.
audits.citation: Marambe D, Rai P. A Prospective Audit Investigating How the Anticholinergic Effect of Medications on Cognition Is Assessed and Reduced in Patients Admitted to an Older Adult Ward in a Psychiatric Hospital. BJPsych Open. 2025;11(S1):S255-S256. doi:10.1192/bjo.2025.10630.

audits.title: Audit: Anticholinergic Burden in Patients Newly Referred to the Central Aberdeenshire CMHT (Feb 2024–Feb 2025)
audits.standard: Documented intervention to review or mitigate anticholinergic medication when ACB score is 3 or more
audits.setting: Central Aberdeenshire Community Mental Health Team, new GP referrals of older adults

cycle1.result: 73% on at least one anticholinergic; 32.7% (N=69) had ACB 3 or more. 75.4% of these had no documented intervention; deprescribing 8.7%, dose reduction 8.7%, medical review suggested 4.4%, switch 2.9%.

audits.intervention: None reported yet; recommended routine ACB calculation at assessment, prompted medication review for ACB 3 or more and targeted education. Re-audit planned.
audits.other_findings: ACB 3 or more in 63.9% of those on eight or more medicines vs 11.8% on fewer than five. Documented interventions had declined compared with previous local audits.
audits.citation: Lee T, Tan J. Audit: Anticholinergic Burden in Patients Newly Referred to the Central Aberdeenshire CMHT (Feb 2024–Feb 2025). BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S168-S169. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11416.

audits.title: Audit of Anticholinergic Burden (ACB) in Intellectual Disability Psychiatry Patients
audits.standard: Best practice for medication review and side-effect monitoring using the ACB Scale
audits.setting: Five community intellectual disability psychiatry teams, Pennine Care NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Medication indication documented 100% in two boroughs but as low as 7.7% in others; cognition monitored in 44.5%; LUNSERS documented in 0.7%; anticholinergic side effects mentioned in 7.5%.

audits.other_findings: 15.1% of the cohort had documented hallucinations.
audits.citation: Bethina L, Patil D, Younes I, Wala E, zia W. Audit of Anticholinergic Burden (ACB) in Intellectual Disability Psychiatry Patients. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S282-S282. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11744.

audits.title: Are medications with anti-cholinergic properties prescribed and reviewed appropriately on a male older person's organic ward?
audits.standard: Reduced ACB score at discharge in 80%; documented consideration of anticholinergic properties for new medicines in 100%
audits.setting: Male older person's organic psychiatric ward, Monkwearmouth Hospital, Sunderland

cycle1.result: 27% had reduced ACB score (target 80%); 0% documentation for 9 new anticholinergic medicines (target 100%).

audits.intervention: Regular prescriber meetings with nursing, medical and pharmacy staff calculating anticholinergic burden.
audits.other_findings: 30 patients had no change in ACB score and 5 had an increase. Re-audit recommended after 6 months.
audits.citation: Greenhalgh B, Anwar H, Hedley R, Perkins C, Shaw R. Are medications with anti-cholinergic properties prescribed and reviewed appropriately on a male older person's organic ward?. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(Suppl 1):S79-S80.

audits.title: Assessing the Anticholinergic Burden in the West Memory Assessment Service (MAS)
audits.standard: Anticholinergic burden (ACB) score documented for patients referred to the memory assessment service
audits.setting: West Leeds Memory Assessment Service, Leeds and York Partnership NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: No documented ACB scores at referral; calculated scores varied by tool, with the lowest suggesting 20.4% (n = 10) had a raised ACB score

audits.intervention: Planned: standardised ACB tool for all new referrals and improved awareness across the memory pathway
audits.other_findings: Amitriptyline was the commonest contributor to anticholinergic burden in all three scoring systems. Re-audit planned in 3 months.
audits.citation: Lees R, Alderson J. Assessing the Anticholinergic Burden in the West Memory Assessment Service (MAS). BJPsych Open. 2022;8(Suppl 1):S163-S163.
